name: Universal Self-Consistency (USC)
executive_summary: Extend Self-Consistency to free-form, open-ended generation by having an LLM itself select the most consistent answer among sampled candidates, instead of requiring exact-match answer extraction to vote.
description: Plain Self-Consistency's majority-vote aggregation only works when a final answer can be cleanly extracted and exactly compared across samples (e.g. a numeric answer), which excludes free-form outputs like code, summaries, and open-ended question answering. USC removes that constraint: rather than extracting and voting, it shows all sampled candidates to an LLM judge and asks it to select or synthesize the most consistent one. Matches standard Self-Consistency's performance on math reasoning (where exact-match voting is applicable) while also working on open-ended tasks where the original method simply cannot be applied at all.
when_to_use: Open-ended or free-form generation tasks (code generation, summarization, open QA) where sampled outputs can't be exactly compared for a majority vote.
As a drop-in generalization of Self-Consistency when task type is mixed or unknown in advance.
when_not_to_use: Tasks with a cleanly extractable, exactly-comparable final answer — plain Self-Consistency's cheaper exact-match voting is sufficient and doesn't need an extra judge call.
known_pitfalls: Selection quality depends on the judge LLM's ability to recognize genuine consistency versus superficial similarity across free-form candidates — this is a judge-checkable property, not a verifier-checkable one like exact-match voting.

primary_source.authors: Chen, Aksitov, Alon, Ren, Xiao, Yin, Prakash, Sutton, Wang, Zhou
primary_source.title: Universal Self-Consistency for Large Language Model Generation
